title: dev-code-review review.json — machine review verdict (incl. R3 masking judge)
description: The ratified output of the dev-code-review skill, written to <evid_root>/<key>/review.json. The recipe branches on `verdict` (approve advances, request-changes routes back to dev-fix); `masking` carries the R3 symptom-masking judge's call. Ratified against samples/EXAMPLE-defect-loop/review.json.

verdict.description: The machine verdict the recipe acts on. Masking suspected => request-changes.

masking.description: The R3 masking judge's call: true = the diff greens the test by hiding the symptom (swallowed exception, suppressed log, narrow special-case).

findings.description: Validated findings only (confidence >= 80 discipline). May be empty on a clean approve.

dimension.description: Which specialist raised it (security, performance, framework_patterns, test_coverage, accessibility, architecture, masking).

summary.description: The reviewer's overall rationale — why this verdict.

next_action.description: OPTIONAL hint for the recipe; the router still derives its action from verdict.

attempt.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). Which attempt of this stage produced the artifact, 1-based. Added because the retry audit had to be reconstructed from session transcripts — no artifact recorded its own attempt number, so a retry was indistinguishable from a first pass after the fact. A retry requires transient-failure evidence; a deterministic failure escalates or changes strategy instead of repeating.

retry_reason.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). Why this attempt happened, when attempt > 1 — the flaky-store match, infra error, timeout or oracle exit 2 that justified it.

timing.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). When this stage ran. Costs microseconds to write and is the only way to tell whether a pipeline redesign still holds months later — without it every duration has to be reconstructed from session transcripts, which do not always exist.

judged_blind.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). Did a context that had NOT produced the thing being judged write this artifact? True only when the skill was invoked via Agent with a fresh context. False means the producer graded itself — well-formed, but not an independent verdict.

model.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). The model this ran on. The checker node enforces judge-strength: a judge weaker than the producer it grades yields an invalid verdict, not merely a weaker one.
